task:
Yes, yes. We have something. 
They've got old-school car races going over on planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system. You know, it's a kind of vehicle that rides on four wheels without antigravity. You won't believe it, but they move by the force of hot gas under high pressure in an engine - that technology died out back in the 22nd century. Strange as it may seem, racing these pieces of junk is still popular. Even the gaals and the faes are hooked on them. 
But why am I telling you all this? Heh, not just for the fun of it. What do you say to representing our planet at the annual championship? It starts <Date>? No, no, you won't have to sit in one of this "capsules of death." You'll be head of operations, driver training, finances, ... 
What? Do we need to hire a whole pack of rangers? If you agree, then sign here. If you succeed, then we'll pay you <Money> cr. If that's not good enough, then refuel and get lost!
success:
Wow! It's him! The very man I knew would be a motorsports star! Have you come to thank me that I opened your eyes to your true calling in life? No? Your fee? Well, I guess there are some formalities that remain... 
Okay, sign here, here, there, and on the doors... 
What do you mean why?" In the past, your signatures were squiggles that merely served to let the pelengs hustle you into your latest predicament. But it's not a signature anymore - it's an autograph. Well, that's everything then. Here are you <Money> cr., <Player>!
loc.1.0:
You didn't have any trouble reaching the western outskirts of town where the stadium was located. The enormous structure left you a bit dumbfounded - you had expected to see an open track. Judging by everything, this is a complete racing complex.
Not far from the entrance you were met by an elderly man who introduced himself as Klim Igorych. He's your team mechanic and will do all in his power to help you hammer out your upcoming victory.
loc.2.0:
Klim Igorych chuckled and moved toward the taxi stop. On the way to the races he described the work you were facing: "The races are between vehicles with an internal combustion engine, four tires, and a steering wheel. A race consists of three heats, the team being represented by one of the drivers in each of them. The same driver can't participate in two different heats. But the components on the race car are the same in all of the heats. Except for the fact that on the final heat you can claim to have defective parts (here Klim smiled slyly) and screw something else on. The track is simple enough, but it's full of changes in the roadway - so you have to tell the driver what to do during the race. By the way, there are five teams in all, one for each race. Your boys don't have much experience, but they sure are talented kiddos. Michael Schulmann himself said they have every chance." 
"I'd be better off driving myself," you thought, remembering how well you drive a foncer. 
At last, you arrived. Klim led you into the holy of holies of any team: the pits - where future champion stallions are shoed up... But what the heck are you talking about? Stallions? This isn't horseracing...
A dark passage under the grandstands led to the pits.
loc.3.0:
"Hey, Igorych, can you tell me in more detail what exactly I'm supposed to do?"
"I already told you," said the mechanic, raising his eyes in surprise. "Choose cars, equip them, come up with a strategy for the race, and then make sure everything goes according to plan. "As easy as fondling a gas tank," said Klim with a loud laugh. But then he suddenly grabbed at his heart. "Something's not right with me...oh, well. It'll pass in a sec. You keep asking questions. Maybe it will help us win in the end."
loc.3.1:
"There's no way! We don't even know what we're driving, and his ideas for a name... There's the freak now," said Igorych.
"What do you mean we don't know?" you asked, feeling taken aback. 
"Just like that. We don't know." There's hardly any money. And we don't have a permanent sponsor. It's one brand, then another... So we need to choose our cars right now. And a name to fit the wheels."
loc.3.2:
"No problem.  Svyatogor Korchenitsa is our star. And then there's Hamilton Dudochkin and Edward Pollonso. Also not bad. They're just really young; it won't work. They're fast devils, can defeat anyone.
"Just as long as they don't drive themselves away," you replied. Igorych nodded in agreement.
loc.3.3: "Don't overlook what we've already got!", laughed Klim. "We're swimming in that goodness. I just wish we had money. Of course, sponsors will give us some, but it's not likely to be enough to buy everything. We have virtually no resources of our own. The last manager was a big shot, like you, friend. He destroyed everything that was good on our team. We've been to the races before, you know," Igorych growled and acted as if he were driving a car. In fact, he performed his racing skit for several minutes.
loc.3.4: "If they're too tough to crack, then we'll crush them! We just need to ice four teams. And then we'll be in with riches instead of being in with witches, like usual. The maloqs are racing super-powered BMUUs: they've got remarkable responsiveness and their engine - it's like on a spaceship - but their drivers are certified numbskulls. The pelengs are on who the hell knows what. They've all got brains and accessories galore. What's more, they know how to cut you off and block the road - just be extra careful with them. How good it is that you can't buy off the timekeeper. ("That's a shame, Klimmy, a real shame!" you thought.) And only a super team can stand up to the FAE-rarri. Engineered throughout...perfect machines. I was talking about the drivers, heh, heh. Shrewd, exact, direct - like I was in my younger days. But, look, their engines run a little starved for oxygen - EURO regulation number thirty seven...no, forty two...bah, I don't remember anymore. And the gaalians - that's a Seetroyan. Their best driver is Baastian Boo-el. He's one of the fastest in the galaxy. But we can find a strategy for all of them. Yes, we... Yes, you... Eh..."
loc.3.5:
"Hey, fella. What's up? Are you overheated?" asked Klim, looking at you somewhat flabbergasted. 
"It's just that most of the things I've gotten involved in have ended like this, if not worse. We could really do without the hellish cars and killer robots."
"Yep," nodded the mechanic.
loc.3.6:
"Why? First, you win - then you celebrate!" Klim replied.
"Yeah, I usually go to bars: sometimes it's an interesting date with a peleng, sometimes - a school buddy, then some gaal hands out stimulants... Too bad! Anyway, I'll have to go myself...
Igorych apparently didn't fully understand what you were saying, so he maintained a high level of respect for you.
loc.4.0: The pits were housed in a large room, albeit nearly empty. There were tools hanging on the walls, a computer in the corner...and that was it. There were no cars, no hoods, and none of the other necessary odds and ends. Like race car drivers, for example. You glanced at Klim Igorych quizzically.
loc.4.1:
You stopped torturing Igorych and walked the rest of the way in silence.
The pits were housed in a large room, albeit nearly empty. There were tools hanging on the walls, a computer in the corner...and that was it. There were no cars, no hoods, and none of the other necessary odds and ends. Like race car drivers, for example. You glanced at Klim Igorych quizzically.
loc.5.0: "To hell with these races," you stammered as you took as you sat down in the driver's seat.  But the reward is irretrievably lost...
loc.7.0:
"Earlier you didn't really want to talk to me... Weasel your own way out of it, genius."
Your only friend here seems to be the computer.  For some reason, it sometimes seems your alter-ego in a parallel world doesn't break away from it much...
You turned on your silicon friend and after some time you beheld the startup screen for the ubiquitous Maloqsoft operating system. You quickly connected to the network that linked the stadium's various rooms. Among them were pits and commentator booths as well as branch offices for car makers and parts manufacturers. Then you received a message from the government of <FromPlanet> saying that a million credits had been transferred to the team's account. <clr>As soon as you get one car in order, the rest will be equipped as well. In other words, you only need to spend this money on buying and outfitting one race car; your employer will pay for the rest. <clrEnd> Clearly, they're afraid of putting all of the money into your hands.
What are you going to do?
loc.7.1: "The guys are getting closer to the start line. Right now they're getting massages. And the cars... We've got to quickly figure out which rides we're taking to this race and how we're going to run them. Here's the terminal; call the manufacturers. Don't worry. They always have cars on the ready for dopes like us. They're right here in the spare pits. So you hurry and order, and I'll clue you in if there's something you don't understand."
loc.8.0:
You began searching for a suitable make for your team. It turns out you can only quickly get three identical cars from a few manufacturers. After reviewing the writeups on the cars, you noticed several suitable options that were accompanied by detailed descriptions:
- <clr>Studebumper<clrEnd> - the car of choice for a young racer! Powerful and maneuverable, this inexpensive car can accommodate even the most severe customization! Minimum outlay, maximum return. Cost: <clr>150,000 cr.<clrEnd>
- <clr>Betta Julietta<clrEnd> - Faithful, like Juliet; uncompromising, like Hamlet. Capable of reaching inhuman (as well as inmaloq and infaeyan) speeds. Equipped with an electronic fuel consumption controller and twenty-two safety airbags. Cost - <clr>250-000 cr.<clrEnd>
- <clr>Gator Piston<clrEnd> - a bullet on the road. Unparalleled handling and acceleration. An ultrafast beast for training drivers. As a gift, your purchase includes a "Always first" sticker and the book "Mental Training for Champions." Cost - <clr>350,000 cr.<clrEnd>
The marketing text didn't give you a proper impression, and you know almost nothing about the cars' performance. Acting without thinking is becoming a habit after a couple of decades of ranger flights. 
Igorych is obviously waiting for some sort of decision. Perhaps it's time to get some clarification.
loc.8.1:
You called Igorych over. His eyes narrowed as they ran across the text on the screen. Then they wandered thoughtfully from corner to corner, and then he said,
"The <clr>Studebumper<clrEnd> is only for saving money. The replacement parts are cheaper for them, as well as the vehicle inspection... And they're simple, like a maloq ABC-book. But their reliability and acceleration is below average. Quite a bit below. Though, again, you can test it out... The <clr>Betta<clrEnd> isn't bad at all. It can do a lot. Just don't get delusional because of its awesome features. The <clr>Alligator<clrEnd> really is sharp-toothed. Few can beat it... It looks so freakin' awesome standing there... I'll just ask, did you talk to GE? They've got these guys there like Mikhael Cheater and Madman Ross with ranger Gamma. Anyway, you can get even scarier stuff there. The latest model of the <clr>Soobaru<clrEnd>, for example. It's true, it'll cost you - <clr>five hundred thousand<clrEnd>, if I remember correctly - but for that it's ready for use, so to speak. Yeah, they've always got a few loaded cars in stock.
loc.8.2: You sent the order and in a moment the cars will be delivered.
loc.8.3: You scolded your mechanic long and loud for not being prepared for the race, for the incivility and disorder in the galaxy, and denounced him as a dominator spy. You felt better; the same couldn't be said about Klim. He was clearly offended and left to the utility room to wipe off the team's only prize cup, which was won for twentieth place in the first semi-real league.
loc.10.0:
Soon, three brand-spanking-new <clr>Studebumpers<clrEnd> were driven into the pits. They didn't look especially attractive, but they had saved the team a lot of money, which you still hadn't learned how to print. The only thing that impressed you was the color of the cars. They were all an identical gray with light blue-green shimmer...you just couldn't figure out what that sort of paint job was supposed to symbolize.
Enough. You had shaken off the problems with the make of the race cars. And there was even money left for some customizations. Time to take on the exhaust pipe... As in upgrading the sports cars.
In front of you is a screen with the accessories being sold today by the car shops located in the stadium structure.
loc.10.1:
You saw the <clr>Betta Juliettas<clrEnd> for the first time, and they didn't disappoint: splendid exterior and comfy interior. If it weren't for the several-thousand-fold difference in power, you might have swapped your spaceship for a car like that. But they were simply wonderful junkers.
Enough. You had shaken off the problems with the make of the race cars. And there was even money left for some customizations. Time to take on the exhaust pipe... As in upgrading the sports cars.
loc.10.2:
The <clr>Gator Piston<clrEnd> is really something. The short, bright yellow cars were shaped like a gaalian pirate ship. It's like launching a nozzle-tipped rocket, but there's nothing close to it: not even a rocket or a nozzle. There were only three superb cars that needed two racing stripes.
Enough. You had shaken off the problems with the make of the race cars. And there was even money left for some customizations. Time to take on the exhaust pipe... As in upgrading the sports cars.
loc.10.3:
Surprisingly, the cars you ordered were quickly delivered. You probably should have asked for something more. Collectable mugs or something like that. You cars are called <clr>Soobaru WRX STI SBR VO<clrEnd>s - the very name that your team represents. Let's just hope that the long name doesn't scare off your fans. Though true connoisseurs will immediately know what's hidden under this moniker. We're talking about explosive acceleration, perfect handling, and complete reliability. But you still want to put some finishing touches of your own on it after the experts at GE, right?
Enough. You had shaken off the problems with the make of the race cars. And there was even money left for some customizations. Time to take on the exhaust pipe... As in upgrading the sports cars.
loc.10.4:
The screen began to blink; then there were blue bars. That's the downside of Maloqsoft software, you know. In the end, you were able to wrest some good information from the computer about all of the parts.
Each part has 6 properties: <clr>speed boost, acceleration boost, handling improvement, weight, reliability, and terrain crossing capacity.<clrEnd> They are listed in parentheses after the name. If a value is preceded by a minus sign, then the part has a negative impact. The exception to this rule is weight. For weight, it's the opposite: the less, the better. In addition to the properties' numeric values, you can also review the part descriptions, which were, of course, constructed by the manufacturers themselves.
1. <clr>Set of pistons made from dominator materials. (S:+8, A:+8, H:0, W:-20, R:+4, T:0) <clrEnd> - Pistons manufactured from kelleroid scrap metal give a car truly heavenly abilities, and to the driver they give confidence that he won't fly off into a black hole...
2. <clr>Wosh Electronics (S:+2, A:+2, H:0, W:0, R:-5, T:0) <clrEnd> -  Doesn't your car needs brains? A car's IQ doesn't exceed 85, which makes it impossible to lose control.
3. <clr>Titanium cylinder block made from quark bomb casings. (S:+12, A:+12, H:0, W:+50, R:-10, T:0) <clrEnd> - The power of the quark under your hood...
4. <clr>Instant cylinder reboring kit. (S:+2, A:+2, H:0, W:-40, R:-15, T:0) <clrEnd> - Don't have time or money? Our superkit will give you decent results at a minimum price.
5. <clr>Carbon-fiber body set. (S:0, A:0, H:0, W:-120, R:0, T:0 ) <clrEnd> - Slightly-outdated, pink faeyan carbon, but it's light and easy just the same! The only thing easier is fulfilling security missions!
6. <clr>Spoilers for your doors, trunk, hood, side panels, and driver. (S:0, A:0, H:0, W:+40, R:+4, T:0) <clrEnd> - They protect both against inadvertent lift-off as well as minor collisions.
7. <clr>Aerodynamic "Fear Bone" body kit. (S:+2, A:0, H:0, W:+20, R:-3, T:-4) <clrEnd> - Wanna look stylish and frightful at the same time? Right this way! Buy a body kit and we'll include a slot for an external scanner as a gift!
8. <clr>RAMBO clutch. (S:0, A:+4, H:0, W:0, R:+4, T:0) <clrEnd> - It's simply the most reliable and technologically advanced clutch in the galaxy, except for the clutch on maloq mass-produced cars - they have different specifications...
9. <clr>Seven-speed manual transmission. (S:+6, A:+10, H:0, W:0, R:0, T:0) <clrEnd> - Do you want to accelerate quickly?  Do you hold electronics in contempt? Then you just don't have any other choice!
10. <clr>Seven-speed automatic transmission. (S:+6, A:+14, H:0, W:0, R:-5, T:0) <clrEnd> - Freedom for your right hand and left foot!
11.  <clr>Terron-style, elastic suspension bar (S:0, A:0, H:+4, W:+40, R:0, T:0) <clrEnd> - Stable, like Terron. Handles like his onboard computer.
12. <clr>PherMacson struts. (S:0, A:0, H:+6, W:+40, R:0, T:-2)<clrEnd> - A true classic.
13. <clr>Hydraulic, hypersensitive chassis. (S:0, A:0, H:+10, W:+30, R:-4, T:+6) <clrEnd> - Navigates most terrains and handles perfectly. Guard against maloq mechanics and peleng distributors!
14. <clr>Maloq-made coil spring booster. (S:0, A:0, H:0, W:+100, R:+12, T:+4) <clrEnd> - Nothing is forever... Well, almost nothing!
15. <clr>SPACE Razor alloy rims. (S:+2, A:+2, H:+2, W:-10, R:0, T:0) <clrEnd> - Rims shaped like the Crystal Chakra.
16. <clr>SPACE Razor alloy rims (XL). (S:+2, A:+2, H:+2, W:-10, R:0, T:+2)<clrEnd> - Exclusive offer! By increasing the radius by 5 centimeters, the diameter increases by 10!
17. <clr>Dr. Maloq forged rims.(S:+3, A:+3, H:+3, W:0, R:-4, T:+2) <clrEnd> - Rims shaped like the Saab Medal. You've never seen anything like these before!
18. <clr>StownBridge racing slicks. (S:+3, A:+3, H:+3, W:0, R:0, T:-2) <clrEnd> - Superfast tires for great roads.
19. <clr>Classic medium tires (S:+2, A:+2, H:+2, W:0, R:0, T:0) <clrEnd> - You can't find more ordinary tires!
20. <clr>GoodDay tires (S:0, A:0, H:0, W:0, R:0, T:+4) <clrEnd> - Got wet roads? Bad roads? No roads at all?
loc.10.5: You scolded your mechanic long and loud for not being prepared for the race, for the incivility and disorder in the galaxy, and denounced him as a dominator spy. You felt better; the same couldn't be said about Klim. He was clearly offended and left to the utility room to wipe off the team's only prize cup, which was won for twentieth place in the first semi-real league.
loc.10.6:
You quickly found records of some kind. Leaving out personal information (which is a must - you've got to maintain the rangers' highly morale image; oh, and Igorych is watching), what remains is as follows:
...who knew that, <clr>even if a car is fully loaded, they would still aggressively market unnecessary parts<clrEnd>, so much money was invested, but it was irrational...This hyped-up, super-charged gimmickry - titanium gobbledygook for an engine - it all went to hell and any-which-way, and then there was the explosion that took the crazy-expensive hydraulics with it. The dominator pistons had worked just fine before. Now I'll have to buy a new body kit, rims... It's true, an overabundance of non-standard parts can really mess up a car! I'll get the carbon body and the space razors again... but they're reliable, as opposed to this freak of a car. You accelerate, it accelerates - but not for long. If you run fast, you'll bow often... The same with that moronic new oil. It's completely useless!
...yesterday I ordered my drivers to be locked out of the cars to keep them from drag racing on the streets. They'll be totaled before the competition. The system with the wires is plain and simple... It's like they say: you come to the races <clr>green<clrEnd>, train until you turn <clr>blue<clrEnd> to avoid going <clr>white<clrEnd> from fear and <clr>red<clrEnd> from stress on the track - until you finish. And the finish line on the final lap is always <clr>black<clrEnd>... Actually, that last part is mine...to help me remember...
loc.10.7: You got mildly tired of all the fuss over hardware selection, but there's room for improvement. Or have you had enough tinkering with cars?
loc.12.0: In this part of the menu, you found engines and car bodies for sale. The prices here really bite - like hungry pachvarashes - but it's hard to overstate the importance of these parts.
loc.12.1: "Order received. Please wait," came the reply from the other side of the screen.
loc.13.0: The second part of the menu, which you are looking at now, is dedicated to transmissions and suspensions. This is the link between car and driver, and car and road, so be extremely careful!
loc.13.1: "Order received. Please wait," came the reply from the other side of the screen.
loc.14.0: The third part of the menu. This is all about wheels: rims and rubber. Oh, if only you could know the weather in advance...
loc.14.1: "Order received. Please wait," came the reply from the other side of the screen.
loc.18.1: The guys from PelengHack brought the part in right away - and they didn't forget to tell you that they didn't know you and that you had never heard anything about them. Further, they asked you to delete your network viewer's log...
loc.18.2: For some reason this part reminded you of how transitory existence can be... You're just flying along, minding your own business, and then somebody's selling your favorite stuff... At least it's not your military awards!
loc.20.0:
"Okay, that's enough! It's high time we started doing something else," you declared with a wise look and stood up from the computer. 
"Igorych, inspect the cars and summon the drivers. I still haven't seen them with my own eyes, and we really need a frictionless team!
Igorych obediently headed off to inspect the cars. He soon reported that everything was in order, that the measurements for the cars' configuration were all within their normal ranges. 
In another half an hour, the race car drivers appeared. You quickly introduced yourself and prepared to assign each of them to a heat. But just then the most experienced of your drivers, Svyatogor Korchenitsa, who was famous for his family connection with a famous foncer rider, announced that they had already divvied up the heats. You didn't start arguing with him, as you really didn't have a clue how well any of them drove.
The adjacent pits were soon crawling with the other teams' mechanics and drivers. You caught a glimpse of the maloqs attaching another sheet of armor to the bumper, while the pelengs were screwing some sort of specialized headlights into place. You couldn't get into the faeyan or gaalian pits, but Korchenitsa was able to sneak in. He informed you that this time the faes were preparing cars with super handling and the gaals were emphasizing the reliability of their machines. It looks like an easy hayride around the racetrack isn't going to materialize.
When they announced the start of the race, you realized that you were just as perturbed as you were during the battle for the system. Korchenitsa volunteered to drive first.
And there they were - all five cars standing at the start line. You were using your computer to keep track of everything that was happening. Igorych and the drivers were standing nearby. The mechanic was clenching some sort of plank in his hands. Your head sported the latest gobzaurus-leather headset, which you would be using to communicate with the driver during the race. Basically, everything was about to begin!
loc.20.1: "This isn't a plank! It's a pit board. They were used to show the driver the time and stuff like that when two-way radios were inadequate. And right now it's our good luck charm, got it?" said Igorych.
loc.20.2: You felt more confident, but it's unlikely that this will bring any real benefit.
loc.23.0:
You checked the communication channel with Korchenitsa and froze in expectation. Yellow circles lit up on the scoreboard, and the drivers started their engines. The roar of the maloq cars nearly drowned out the din of the stadium through which the starting and ending legs of the track passed. The middle leg runs along a specially-prepared, unpaved section of the track.
As soon as the scoreboard turned green, the race cars zipped from their places. Now it's time to give Korchenitsa instructions for getting through the first stage - an asphalt speedway that's loaded with turns. The driver is waiting for your instructions.
loc.24.0: "Aye, aye, sir!" sounded Svyatogor's voice in your headset as you lost direct sight of his race car. Now you'll have to switch to "instrument flight rules": the computer screen and two-way radios. You decided to not distract the driver and simply watch the first leg for a bit.
loc.25.0:
Korchenitsa squeezed everything he could out of the car. There was a spot where he could have pulled into the lead, but the faeyan driver quickly blocked him in a deft move that seriously complicated Svyatogor's life. But the outcome wasn't so bad. There's always hope for a good sequel!
One after another, the cars left the confines of the stadium. Now the race is crossing the unpaved road with small pits in some places. You need to give Korchenitsa new instructions ASAP!
loc.25.1: Svyatogor drove the race car carefully but with verve. But he trailed slightly behind the gaals, who were leading, and was forced to tussle with the peleng driver, who was trying over and over again to knock Korchenitsa off course.
loc.25.2: Following your instructions, Korchenitsa used the car's racing capabilities with extreme caution and wound up at the end of the pack. But it's not over yet!
loc.26.0: Igorych's beard was twitching nervously next to you. You were a little concerned, but completely in control of the situation. And somewhere out on the racetrack your driver was battling for victory. It had been quite a long time since you had such a nerve-wracking day - probably not since the final operation to liberate the system.
loc.27.0:
Following your instructions, the driver proved himself rather competent on this section. At least, everything that you told him to do, he did. This left you pleased, but maybe it would have been better to drive. If only you were the one behind the wheel...
Igorych brought you back from your daydreams by reminding you that the drivers were approaching the third stage - a true offroad experience. What advise are you going to give Korchenitsa?
loc.28.0: That's all. Korchenitsa is on his own now. Until the end of the stage, of course. It's so good that you let him know how his competition is doing on the racetrack.
loc.29.0:
Your team's second driver headed to the track and warmed up the race car before his stage began. Igorych started verifying the communication channel with him. 
Picking up decent speed, the cars flew in, one after another, on the stadium's track, filling the surrounding area with the roar of their engines. The first circuit is coming to an end. It's your last chance to instruct Korchenitsa. What are your orders?
loc.30.0:
Growling and snorting, Korchenitsa's rather thrashed race car barreled along toward the finish line. You were carefully following the scene, when Igorych jabbed you in the side with his elbow:
"It's...uh...it's totally...do you understand?"
"What?"  you asked, not comprehending what your mechanic was trying to explain to you. But you could sense from his face, which had rapidly gone pale, that it wasn't anything good. And right you were.
"We've lost communication with the second car! The boy's driving without contact with us! Think of it! Blind! What are we going to do?!"
You began to think and convulse. You've got to find a way to communicate with the driver or his performance isn't going to be so hot...
loc.30.1: Igorych endured your dressing-down without grumbling, but he was visibly offended.
loc.31.0:
You ran headlong toward the racetrack, expecting to think up something specific to do once you were on the track. It seemed to you that you were moving faster than the gaalian race cars, and when it occurred to you that you weren't expending even a drop of gasoline, you experienced utter bliss. Your pleasant fantasy was interrupted by a maloq mechanic who was unexpectedly blocking your path. 
"Where're you goin'? Only drivers and mechanics can be on the track. None of you directors and mangy managers are allowed!" snarled the maloq.
loc.31.1:
"Listen, you miserable creep! I, the great <Ranger>, should be on the track already, and if you don't get out of my sight this instant, I'll just have to terminate your career as a guard and begin your glorious life as an invalid!
"Go right ahead," replied the maloq calmly after gently bumping you away from the track entrance with his belly.
loc.32.0: You tore out of there and dashed to a commentator booth. The stadium employees you encountered along the way looked at you curiously; team leaders don't usually act this way during a race. But you didn't care what they thought, your team was on the edge of a catastrophe. After repeatedly cursing the broken hyperlift and the length of the stairs, you reached the highest point in the stadium. Kicking the door wide, you burst into the booth. The startled commentators looked at you, dumbfounded. What do you do?
loc.33.0: You asked for forgiveness and left, this time carefully closing the door. The road back to the pits seemed like an eternity. When it stopped, you and Korchenitsa carried Igorych straight to the operating room, explaining just what had happened to the doctors that came running up. The smoldering Lambo plummeted downward suddenly along with the elevator which was unable to continue to support its weight. If didn't dare think of what would have been if that had happened half a minute earlier...
You were ordered out of the operating room, leaving behind Igorych and, unexpectedly, Svyatogor, who also needed medical attention after riding with you. You took it upon yourself to wait until the end of the operation, but the chief doctor invited you into his office.
He informed you that you'd probably go to prison for violating a hundred rules - but that he was obligated to present you with a reward of <clr>100,000 cr.<clrEnd>, something granted to anybody who saves the life of an intelligent being on <ToPlanet>. 
Considering the cost of the repairs to the hospital, of course, the remaining reward amounts to <clr>2,000 cr.<clrEnd>. He further reassured you about the mechanic and the driver: the first would live; the second just gained a few more gray hairs - no big deal. And he advised you to leave the planet before the law enforcement agencies investigated the aftermath of your heroism.
You left the hospital and headed for the spaceport with a clean conscious: mission accomplished and Igorych saved. It just took you a long time to get there - you walked, because at this point any type of vehicle made you nauseous..

You heard Svyatogor's voice, as if from a great distance:
"Too late, Boss. He's...he's dead..."

Igorych's voice sounded into your headset:
"Boss, they finished! The gaalians won! It's over!"
You pulled back on your speed and calmly drove to the finish line. The important thing now is to forget this defeat as quickly as possible and never show your face on <FromPlanet> again.
Reassuring yourself with these words, you made your way back to the spaceport and returned to your ship.
